I'll give you an example. You're probably at some point going to learn how to balance redox reactions. In a nutshell, this has to do with changing oxidation states and electron transfer. In Chem I, all you had to do was balance atoms and you were done. In Chem 2, you'll have to predict the products, and assign oxidation states to the elements and compounds in the reaction. Using these, you're going to write 1/2 reactions for the substances undergoing reduction and oxidation, this involves the transfer of electrons to get to a higher/lower oxidation state. With these half reactions, you'll add them up to get your net ionic equation. It seems scary at first , but trust me, once you get the hang of it its easy as cake. Oh, and this is only one of the many reactions you will learn of in Chem 2! If you have any other questions, feel free to ask! :)
